chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'aib, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

He wished and willed, and He did not love nor become pleased. I said to him: How? He said: He wished that there should not be anything except with His Knowledge, and He willed the same as that, and He did not love that it is said to Him: 'The third of three', and He was not pleased with disbelief for His servants.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God's wish, will, love, and pleasure according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the theological distinction between divine volition and affection, clarifying that God's 'wishing' and 'willing' are intrinsically linked to His all-encompassing Knowledge, whereas His 'not loving' and 'not being pleased' specifically denote His rejection of human disbelief (kufr) and the error of attributing partners to Him (shirk). This hadith serves as a critical exegetical tool in Shia kalām for refuting the Mu'tazilite and Sunni interpretations that conflate divine will with desire, affirming instead that God's will is always accompanied by wisdom and knowledge, even when He wills what He does not 'love' in the sense of approval.
